# logfire_gateway_endpoint (Resource)

Manages an organization-owned AI Gateway endpoint and the providers it routes to. Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read_gateway and organization:write_gateway scopes (organization:read and organization:write are also accepted). Endpoints that use built-in providers or more than 100 providers are not supported. Import accepts the endpoint UUID or its organization-unique slug.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "logfire_gateway_endpoint" "default" {
  slug        = "default"
  description = "Prefer OpenAI and fall back to Anthropic."

  providers = [
    {
      provider_id = logfire_gateway_provider.openai.id
      priority    = 10
    },
    {
      provider_id = logfire_gateway_provider.anthropic.id
    },
  ]
}
```

## Routing

`providers` is the complete set of providers the endpoint routes to. The Gateway
tries providers with a higher `priority` first. Providers with the same priority
are tried in a random order that follows their `weight`. An inactive provider
stays assigned but receives no requests. At least one provider must be active.

A change to any provider replaces the whole set in one request, so the endpoint
never routes to a partial configuration. Logfire stores `weight` as a 32-bit
float. The provider keeps the configured value when it matches what Logfire stored.

If a routing policy uses a provider, the API refuses to remove or pause it.
Update the routing policy first.

## Failed creates

Creation is not retried automatically. A failed request can still leave an
endpoint stored. Check the endpoint list before retrying. If the slug exists,
import it by slug and apply the configuration again. A conflicting slug is never
adopted automatically.

## Supported configuration

The resource manages endpoints whose providers all belong to the organization.
Endpoints that use a built-in provider, or more than 100 providers, return a
conflict error. Manage those in the Logfire UI.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `providers` (Attributes Set) Complete set of providers the endpoint routes to. A change replaces the whole set in one request. At least one provider must be active. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--providers))
- `slug` (String) Organization-unique endpoint slug. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Endpoint description.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the endpoint was created.
- `id` (String) Endpoint UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--providers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `providers`

Required:

- `provider_id` (String) UUID of a `logfire_gateway_provider` in the same organization.

Optional:

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the Gateway routes to this provider. Defaults to true.
- `priority` (Number) The Gateway tries providers with a higher priority first. Providers with the same priority are tried in a random order that follows their weights. Defaults to 0.
- `weight` (Number) Positive relative weight among providers with the same priority. Defaults to 1.

## Import

Import an endpoint by slug or UUID using the same organization's management token:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_gateway_endpoint.default
  id = "default"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# Import an existing Gateway endpoint by its organization-unique slug, or by its UUID.
#
# By slug:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_endpoint.default' "default"

# By UUID:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_endpoint.default' "018f45c0-3cab-7b2f-a8f7-8a0b55a7ed00"
```
